title: Outputs bind snapshot renderers to typed plugin sinks

nodes.summary: Outputs bind KB renderers to configured sinks over one selected root
nodes.detail: An output binds a KB-authored renderer, which may compose dependent queries, to a configured sink connector whose input type it produces; every read uses the same selected root. Browsing never updates an external output, sink invocation needs no evolution, and changing an output definition or sink configuration is an ordinary evolution.

realised.evidence: No output, renderer or sink code exists in kyyn-v2 at end of history

nodes.summary: One pure snapshot-read form for queries and renderers
nodes.detail: Queries and renderers are KB code, not function-valued facts, and share one registered form returning a SnapshotRead Program interpreted against the selected snapshot; pure calculations are lifted, and SnapshotRead permits no acquisition, sink invocation or publication.
sections: Decision / Root data and authored declarations

realised.evidence: PR #27 implements the shared SnapshotRead Program algebra for queries (renderers never built)

nodes.summary: Output GADT pairs renderer with a generated typed SinkBinding
nodes.detail: `Output` takes the renderer function and a generated `SinkBinding input` that cannot be forged from a source connector or mismatched sink; KbDefinition holds existential SomeQuery/SomeOutput lists from which generated registration supplies names, contracts and codecs.
sections: Decision / Root data and authored declarations

realised.evidence: SinkBinding/KbDefinition/SomeOutput never appeared in code (the 'Output' identifier at seq 6 is unrelated)

nodes.summary: Queries stay independently callable via queryRoot on a Validated root
nodes.detail: queryRoot runs a query by descriptor and checked arguments against a Validated Root, with RootExecution checking contracts, so Web/MCP can show structured results without a renderer or sink and without reimplementing calculations in JS.

realised.evidence: queryRoot code_added at seq 26 over structurally checked roots; the Validated Root gate arrives at seq 27 (PR #28)

nodes.summary: prepareOutput checks renderer result against the sink's input contract
nodes.detail: Preparation evaluates the renderer in RootExecution (no PluginInvocation) and checks its result against the sink binding resolved from the same root. PreparedOutput is an ordinary, unretained value; a later update may re-render and need not reproduce a preview.

nodes.summary: Large payloads use immutable ArtifactStore references
nodes.detail: Large file/document inputs may reference immutable artifacts (bytes plus media type) that must resolve to fixed bytes or fail; this is optional, not a universal document conversion, and no generic Destination type is added.

nodes.summary: Delivery capability explicitly invokes sinks and records outcomes
nodes.detail: A host Delivery effect (InvokeSink, InspectDelivery) lowers to PluginInvocation and filesystem plumbing, persists dispatch intent before acting and validates results. The first file sink is a first-party plugin whose relative paths resolve against the KB directory; normal updates use an accepted snapshot.

realised.evidence: No Delivery effect or sink plugin exists; PluginInvocation (seq 78) serves acquisition only

nodes.summary: Sink failures: idempotency per sink, Uncertain outcomes, no rollback
nodes.detail: Sinks declare idempotent replacement versus non-idempotent actions; pre-dispatch failures are distinct from Uncertain dispatch, which is never silently retried, and sink failure cannot roll back accepted knowledge or external effects.

realised.evidence: No delivery outcome types in code ('Acknowledged' at seq 92 is curation, unrelated)

nodes.summary: Generated per-KB Query alias; renderers are `args -> Query input`
nodes.detail: The query/renderer form becomes the SDK Query monad specialised by a generated `type Query a = SDK.Query Root a`; the root is implicit and queries compose directly in do-notation instead of threading an explicit root.
sections: Decision / Root data and authored declarations

realised.evidence: PR #27 generates the root-specific Query alias and collection bindings

nodes.summary: queryRoot returns QueryResult with an ordered read trace
nodes.detail: Query invocation returns the checked result together with the ordered snapshot-read trace from ADR 0009, laying ground for future query explanation without committing to a predicate language.

realised.evidence: QueryResult code_added at seq 26; PR #27 returns ordered traces

nodes.summary: Outputs registered in kb.dhall naming renderer export and sink reference
nodes.detail: Instead of an authored Output GADT and SinkBinding, outputs are kb.dhall entries naming a renderer export and a plugin/instance/method SinkReference. The host inspects both signatures and generates an adapter that type-checks renderer result against sink input; the manifest is the authority.
sections: Decision / Root data and authored declarations

realised.evidence: No output registration, OutputDefinition or SinkReference exists in code

editorial.note: Also flips status to Accepted and adds explicitly non-committal 'future directions' for SQL-like query explanation and host-side execution
Also swaps the status line for front matter and adjusts Verification wording to the named-entry form; metadata/verification only

notes: The output half of this ADR has never been built: every node about renderers, sinks, preparation, delivery, artifacts and failure semantics (0017.01, .03, .05-.08, .11) is unrealised at the end of history, more than 160 steps after the founding spec. The only realised parts are the query mechanics this ADR shares with 0008/0009 (seq 26). Even so, seq 143 redesigned the unbuilt output declaration, replacing the authored Output GADT, SinkBinding and existential KbDefinition with kb.dhall named-entry registration, so that it matches how queries and tools ended up being registered. That is a spec-only rewrite of a spec-only design. The Delivery/Invoking-the-sink and Failure-behavior sections are still the founding text, untouched. The seq 26 'future directions' paragraph (SQL-like query explanation, host-side query execution) is explicitly disclaimed as not a commitment, so I left it out of the nodes. Founding Verification demands (Web/MCP queries, HTML preview isolation) produce no nodes.
